news.title: ‘Not today, not here’: Infantino tight-lipped on abandoned World Cup rights proposal
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who attended the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice on Saturday, remained tight-lipped about whether he regrets his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup. The event is the first tournament organised by world soccer's ruling body since the Swiss administrator called off the plan, which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion. The proposal was abandoned in late July following a fierce backlash and boycott threats from regional governing bodies, including Europe's UEFA and major stakeholders in the sport. news.title: Italy overcome stubborn New Zealand at FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have lost their second game at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, conceding three late goals at Stadion Miejski ŁKS in Łódź. Substitutes Rosanna Ventriglia and Karen Appiah made the difference as Italy booked their place in the knockout rounds thanks to a hard-fought 3-0 victory over a stubborn New Zealand side. “We had a plan coming into the game, and I thought for the majority of it, we executed that,” New Zealand head coach Callum Holmes said after the match. “There’s a couple of little areas where we need to be better, and that’s something for us as a team to learn.
